entities.evidence: אֱלֹהִים names God, the speaker who sees the rainbow and remembers his covenant with every living creature. The source tag identifies this bearer as LORD@Gen.1.1.

review.translation: [So|0] [the rainbow|1] [will be|0] [in the cloud|2], [and I will see it|3] [to remember|4] [the|5] [everlasting|6] [covenant|5] [between|7] [God|8] [and|9] [every|10] [living|12] [creature|11] [among all|13] [flesh|14] [that|15] {is} [on|16] [the earth|17].”

analysis.evidence: בֶּעָנָן, “in the cloud,” specifies where the bow will be. The next clause, וּרְאִיתִיהָ, “and I will see it,” refers to the bow present there.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ precedes a Qal perfect third-person feminine singular verb agreeing with הַקֶּשֶׁת, “the bow.” The weqatal form has future reference in the covenant promise.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

draft.change: Assign the occurrence to the existing rainbow sense of קֶשֶׁת under קשת and clarify the evidence from Genesis 9:16.
draft.definition: The coloured arc visible in a cloud.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:16 identifies the bow by its position in the cloud and by God's seeing it as a reminder of the covenant with every living creature.

analysis.evidence: בֶּעָנָן places the bow in the cloud. God says וּרְאִיתִיהָ, “I will see it,” and gives the purpose לִזְכֹּר בְּרִית עוֹלָם, “to remember the everlasting covenant.”
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial ק of the feminine singular absolute noun קֶשֶׁת. The feminine singular verb וְהָיְתָה agrees with it, and the feminine singular suffix in וּרְאִיתִיהָ refers back to it.
analysis.sense: The rainbow visible in the cloud as the sign of the covenant.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67854:7, 67853:3.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ incorporates the definite article before עָנָן, a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: The feminine suffix refers to הַקֶּשֶׁת, the bow in the cloud. God says he will see the bow, and לִזְכֹּר gives the purpose of seeing it, to remember the everlasting covenant.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ precedes a Qal perfect in the first person common singular. The third-person feminine singular suffix הָ is the direct object. The verb continues the promise with future force.

analysis.evidence: God sees the bow in order to remember בְּרִית עוֹלָם, the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature. The bow signals that God will uphold that covenant.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לִ marks purpose before the Qal infinitive construct זְכֹּר. God, the speaker of וּרְאִיתִיהָ (“I will see it”), is also the subject of the infinitive.

analysis.evidence: בְּרִית עוֹלָם means “an everlasting covenant.” God sees the bow in the cloud and remembers this covenant, whose parties the verse identifies as God and every living creature on earth.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state before עוֹלָם, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh

analysis.evidence: In בְּרִית עוֹלָם, עוֹלָם describes how long the covenant endures. God sees the bow and remembers the covenant with every living creature on earth. The verse gives no endpoint for that covenant.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state. It completes the construct phrase בְּרִית עוֹלָם.
analysis.sense: duration with no stated endpoint (in context)

analysis.evidence: After בְּרִית עוֹלָם ‘an everlasting covenant’, בֵּין introduces אֱלֹהִים ‘God’ as one party. The following וּבֵין introduces כָּל נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה ‘every living creature’ as the other.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: In בֵּין אֱלֹהִים וּבֵין כָּל נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, the first בֵּין introduces God and the marked וּבֵין introduces every living creature as the other party to the everlasting covenant (בְּרִית עוֹלָם).
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ ‘and’ prefixes the preposition בֵין ‘between’.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: כָּל governs the singular phrase נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, “living creature.” The covenant is between God and every living creature on earth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, with feminine agreement in חַיָּה. No prefix or suffix.

In בְּכָל בָּשָׂר, “among all flesh,” כָל takes the collective noun בָּשָׂר as its complement. The phrase identifies the whole group to which every living creature in the covenant belongs.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “among.” The noun כָל is masculine singular in the construct state before בָּשָׂר.

analysis.evidence: In בְּכָל בָּשָׂר, “among all flesh,” כָּל gives בָּשָׂר collective scope. The preceding כָּל נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, “every living creature,” identifies the earthly beings included in the covenant.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with collective reference. The initial ב is part of the noun.
analysis.sense: all flesh: every living creature; mankind

analysis.morphology: Indeclinable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר עַל הָאָרֶץ means “that is on the earth.” The phrase describes the dwelling place of all the living creatures included in the covenant.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes אָרֶץ, the pausal form of the common noun אֶרֶץ, singular and absolute. The noun is marked for both genders.
